newsitem.title: USA: Candela to market pain-reducing device.
newsitem.headline: Candela to market pain-reducing device.

text.p: Candela Corp said Tuesday it has received a go-ahead from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market a new device designed to reduce pain during laser surgery.
The company said the instrument, called the Dynamic Cooling Device, is expected to cost less than $20,000. It is scheduled for general availability in mid-1997.
The device is different from other skin-cooling devices because it selectively cools the top layers of skin during laser treatments, the company said.
Candela said that method minimizes thermal injuries and pain without decreasing the effectiveness of laser treatments.
